mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically each week for the past three weeks (-13.7 to -10.9), indicating a steady recovery trend in discretionary mobility that is likely to continue into the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the mean over the last 28 days despite the prior monotonic weekly improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week recovery in WORKPLACES mobility (from -9.3 to -3.7) reflects resumed commuting and office-adjacent errands, which should feed through to higher retail and recreation footfall within one to two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -9.3 at t-2w to -3.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 1-2 weeks even though WORKPLACES continues to improve.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility rebounds above a -5 point threshold (it is currently at -5.3 and improving), this signals renewed willingness to travel for non-essential purposes, which should push RETAIL_REC upward within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -5 points from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -9.4 at t-2w to -5.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses above -5 but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (staying near +6 to +7 percent above baseline, with no clear downward trend) indicates persistent home-anchoring behavior that caps discretionary outings, dampening any rise in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 6.0 and 7.3 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining flat or elevated above 6 percent.

mechanism_narrative: The joint improvement in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT simultaneously signals a broad-based mobility recovery (commuting plus transit use), which compounds to produce a stronger uplift in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict, over a four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rose from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater than growth predicted from WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, or RETAIL_REC declines despite joint improvement in both series.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high GROCERY_PHARM mobility (above 30 percent and rising to 37.6) combined with declining PARKS mobility suggests a substitution pattern where essential-goods trips are replacing outdoor recreation, which together signal constrained but not expanding discretionary retail activity, keeping RETAIL_REC flat to lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose to 37.6 while PARKS fell to -14.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even as GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated and PARKS remains depressed.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS mobility decline from -12.0 to -17.0 at t-1w followed by partial recovery to -14.6 suggests weather-driven volatility in outdoor activity; if PARKS mobility drops below -18 points in a future week, it signals adverse conditions (e.g. rain season onset in Hong Kong) that would also suppress retail footfall over the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -18 points from baseline in a given week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -17.0 at t-1w, near this threshold
failure_condition: PARKS falls below -18 but RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime where Hong Kong authorities are easing social-distancing restrictions (consistent with simultaneous increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT alongside decreases in RESIDENTIAL growth), RETAIL_REC should continue its upward trajectory over the next four weeks as pent-up demand is released; this mechanism is conditional on continued policy easing rather than a tightening regime.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved and RESIDENTIAL stabilized near 6.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 4 weeks even as WORKPLACES continues to improve and RESIDENTIAL remains stable, or if restrictions are observed to tighten instead of ease.
